intro_html: Sweet, tangy, salty pad thai with chicken, scrambled egg, and a peanut crunch on top. Each bowl brings 36 grams of protein at 791 calories for about $3.13. That is the most expensive recipe in this stretch of the library, and it is still a quarter of what the Thai place charges.
cost_closing_html: About $3.13 a bowl for chicken pad thai with all the fixings. Restaurant pad thai runs $13 to $16 a plate, so even our priciest noodle bowl saves you around $10 every single serving.
shop_smart: Rice noodles are the big line item at $10.49. If your store has an international aisle or you can hit an Asian market, the same noodles often drop to half the mainstream-brand price.
Fourteen eggs do heavy lifting for protein at only $1.72. Eggs are still one of the cheapest proteins per gram in the store.

Fish sauce, oyster sauce, and lime juice look like a spendy haul, but they are pantry bottles. Counted at what this batch actually uses, they add about a dollar per bowl, then keep flavoring batches for months.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the rice noodles in hot tap water 20 to 30 minutes until pliable but not fully soft, then drain. They finish cooking in the pot.
Stir the sauce together: fish sauce, brown sugar, oyster sauce, and lime juice. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Slice the chicken thin, season with salt and pepper, and sear it in batches in a little of the oil over high heat until cooked through to 165 F. Set aside.
In the same pot, cook the sliced onion and garlic in more oil until fragrant. Push everything to one side, pour in the beaten eggs, and scramble until just set.
Add the drained noodles and the sauce. Toss and fry 2 to 3 minutes, until the noodles soak up the sauce and turn glossy. Return the chicken and toss once more.
Portion into 14 containers and top each with a spoonful of chopped peanuts so they keep their crunch.
portion_html: Put the whole pot on the scale, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Weigh that into each container and split the peanuts on top. Each bowl works out to about 791 calories with 36 grams of protein.

head.keywords: chicken pad thai, pad thai meal prep, thai noodles, budget meal prep, homemade takeout, cheap dinner recipes
steps: Soak rice noodles in hot water until pliable, then drain.
Mix fish sauce, brown sugar, oyster sauce, and lime juice into the pad thai sauce.
Sear sliced chicken to 165 F, then cook onion and garlic and scramble the eggs in the same pot.
Add noodles and sauce, toss until glossy, and return the chicken.
Portion into 14 containers and top with chopped peanuts.
